title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 83
paragraphs: The Greeks, since they now believed what the Tenians reported, were preparing for battle. And as dawn appeared, they held an assembly of those who fought on board the ships and addressed them, Themistocles making a speech that was eloquent beyond the rest. The substance of it was to set forth all that is better as opposed to all that is worse of the various elements that arise in human nature and constitution; and having exhorted them to choose the better, and so bringing his speech to a close, he bade them embark in their ships. These accordingly began to board; and meanwhile the trireme arrived from Aegina that had gone to bring the sons of Aiacos.
